posts.title: Marginalia to Phenomenology of Perception
posts.description: We are like fishes swimming in the sea of sense, bounded above by the superior element, but unable to breathe it pure or penetrate it. —William James, Pragmatism The many-angled houses of my sight are traced from an elusive diagram beyond compulsion, the intangible. posts.title: Opinions
posts.description: There is scarce any Philosopher but dies twice or thrice in Laertius; Nor almost any life without two or three deaths in Plutarch; which makes the tragicall ends of noble persons more favourably resented by compassionate Readers, who finde some relief in the Election of such differences. —Thomas Browne, Urn Burial
